xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-5153: GitHub organizations: resolve the acting identity per repository and show which owner a project belongs to

plan.title: GitHub organizations: resolve the acting identity per repository and show which owner a project belongs to
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5-5

references.label: PAN-5154 (out of scope: per-owner gh accounts, GHES)

metadata.sizeJustification: The operator authored the PRD as one issue with one npm release (highest priority, publish on merge) and asked that nothing be re-decided. The core (W1-W5 plus W13) cannot ship apart: W5 without W13 makes every uncovered repository unmergeable, and W13 without W5 weakens approval with no benefit. The remaining surface (route, doctor, sidebar, chip, settings, docs) all read the one identity resolver from W4 and are small leaves. Most of the file count is test files whose mocks must change with the call sites they cover, plus six doc files the docs gate requires.

narratives.Problem: Overdeck holds one GitHub App installation (the home installation) and treats it as valid for every repository. Sixteen branch points choose the App path with isGitHubAppConfigured(), which only checks that credential files exist, so a repository the App is not installed on (mindyournow/myn-cli, eltmon/krux) takes the App path and fails although the gh path would work. Spawn writes the home token and an HTTPS remote into every workspace; the verdict, check run and commit statuses use the home token; marker approvals count only from the bot when the App is configured, so an uncovered repository could never pass review once verdicts move to the gh user. Reopen and discussion sync call gh against the wrong repository. No UI or CLI shows a project's owner or the identity that acts there.
narratives.Proposal: Ask GitHub which installation covers each repository (GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/installation with the App JWT; positive answers cached in memory for 6h, 404s in repo notes), mint the token for that installation, and choose the App path per repository with appCoversRepo(owner, repo); uncovered repositories take the existing gh path as the signed-in user. A lookup failure other than 404 keeps today's behavior. One resolver (resolveRepoIdentity / collectGitHubIdentities) feeds spawn, GET /api/github/identities, pan doctor rows per owner, collapsible owner groups in the sidebar, an owner · login chip in the Command Deck and a read-only Settings section. On uncovered repositories an APPROVED marker counts from any trusted author, as on a machine without the App. Reopen and discussion sync pass --repo. Docs explain covering an organization (make the App public, install it on the org).
narratives.NonGoals:
- A separate gh account, token or host per owner (work account, Enterprise Managed User, GitHub Enterprise Server, ghe.com): PAN-5154.
- A second GitHub App or per-owner App credential directories.
- Storing an installation id per repository on disk or in projects.yaml.
- Rewriting the origin remote or credential.helper of a repository an earlier spawn already changed; pan doctor only reports it with the fix.
- Any change to the PAT paths (GitHubClient, issue poller, webhook allowlist).
- Per-installation quota pools; all App calls stay in the single app pool, and the installation lookup is not metered.
- Changing isGitHubAppConfigured(), getMergeBackendStatus(), verifyAppCanMerge(), getAppStatus(), the quota sampler, forge-identity.ts or githubPrLookupSource().
- An owner picker in the Add-project dialog or an owner filter in the sidebar.
- Refusing an agent spawn because the identity is user or none.
- Raising any row in scripts/file-size-allowlist.txt, adding Effect wrappers, or a contracts package change.
